subject: Re: Demo + migration goals - OpenAI compatibility & hyperscaler comparison
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Demo + migration goals - next steps

Hi Claire - great to meet earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Recap:
- Primary goals: reduce inference unit cost and get predictable latency for customer-facing features; must preserve OpenAI-compatible behavior for minimal SDK changes.
- Key constraints: data residency in US, SOC2 evidence required, procurement timeline ~4-6 weeks.
- Workloads: chat + few-shot classification + embeddings (search).

Proposed evaluation plan (attached: evaluation-plan.pdf, test-matrix.xlsx):
1) Compatibility smoke tests (API/SDK swap): use your existing OpenAI client in a staging env against Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoint to validate request/response parity and function-calling behavior.
2) Perf/cost comparison: 48-72 hour side-by-side run against your current hyperscaler and OpenAI to capture p95 latency, avg cost/token, and throughput under representative traffic.
3) Prompt diff & quality check: run your key prompts (sample set) and flag any divergences for triage.

Owners & rough timeline:
- Redwood: setup compatibility endpoint + perf harness (Nikhil, 3 business days)
- FinCo: provide sample prompts, representative traffic replay, and security questionnaire (Claire)

Can you confirm: 1) you want us to prioritize OpenAI API parity first; 2) preferred start date (we have availability starting Aug 16)?

Thanks - I'll loop in engineering once you confirm.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Attachment: evaluation-plan.pdf (summary), test-matrix.xlsx (workload matrix)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-11T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo + migration goals - technical checklist

Hi Claire - quick technical checklist to make the SDK-swap and perf tests smooth. I put a short guide together (openai-compat-guide.md) - attaching key points inline below.

Compatibility items:
- Endpoints: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings should accept same payloads (role/contents, messages, functions) and return compatible fields (choices, delta streaming tokens, function_call).
- Headers/Auth: support Bearer token and accept the same rate-limit headers for fair comparison.
- Streaming: ensure chunked transfer with same stop sequences; we support gpt-style streaming with event frames.
- Tokenization: we'll run a tokenizer parity check against your model prompts to flag differences and estimate token delta (cost impact).
- Model mapping: map names to closest Redwood-hosted variants; provide fallback policy for unavailable models.

Perf/cost harness:
- We'll run a 48-hour replay using your traffic sample via the test-matrix.xlsx matrix (ramp-up/scenario definitions).
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency, tail latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-1k-tokens, error rates; we'll produce a side-by-side CSV.

What we need from FinCo:
- Representative sample prompts (CSV) + expected outputs for quality checks.
- A short list of function schemas you use in production.
- Confirm staging host and whether we can accept traffic via a VPN/peering (for private ingress).

I estimate ~3 business days to stand up the endpoint and harness once we have your samples.

-Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai
Attachment: openai-compat-guide.md (details and sample curl/snippets)
